data.name: Bilhah
data.gender_notes: Bilhah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Hebrew Bible, Bilhah is the handmaid of Rachel who bears Jacob two sons, Dan and Naphtali (Genesis 30:3-8). The name Bilhah carries the meaning “Servant girl” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Bilhah usually hope their child will grow to embody servant girl and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion and loyalty to one's master.
data.etymology: Bilhah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant girl.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bilhah total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: בלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם בלה הוא נגזר משורש עברי שפירושו משרת או שפחה. השם מוזכר בתנ"ך ככינויה של אחת מנשותיו של רחל, אשתו של יעקב. בלה היא דמות חשובה בספר בראשית ומהווה דוגמה לאישה נאמנה ומסורה במשפחתה.

in_greek.name: Βαλὰ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βαλὰ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος בלה, που σημαίνει υπηρέτις ή πιστή δουλή. Στη Βίβλο, η Βαλὰ αναφέρεται ως μία από τις υπηρέτριες της Ραχήλ, συζύγου του Ιακώβ, στο βιβλίο της Γένεσης.

in_latin.name: Bilhah
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Bilhah is derived from the Hebrew root meaning 'ministress' or 'faithful servant'. In the Bible, Bilhah is mentioned as one of the handmaids of Rachel, the wife of Jacob, in the book of Genesis. The name signifies a devoted and loyal servant in the biblical context.

in_english.name: Bilhah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bilhah originates from the Hebrew language, meaning 'faithful servant' or 'handmaid'. It is biblically significant as the name of one of Rachel's handmaids in the book of Genesis. The name symbolizes loyalty, devotion, and humility, reflecting the character of the biblical figure. In Christian tradition, Bilhah is recognized as a symbol of faithful service and commitment to family and community.

data.cultural_impact: Bilhah's name comes from the Hebrew root "b-l-h" meaning "devouring, swallowing, or gorging," possibly alluding to her role as a surrogate mother who helped Rachel conceive children.
data.spiritual_significance: Bilhah's story represents the love and support given by women to each other, as well as the power of faith and prayer. Rachel, in her deep longing for a child and her trust in Bilhah's ability to bear a son, demonstrates the connection between hope, determination, and divine intervention. Bilhah's willingness to carry the seed of her master, Jacob, symbolizes the power of sacrifice, selflessness, and strong bonds within a community. Additionally, Bilhah's descendent tribes, Dan and Naphtali, show that even in challenging circumstances, new opportunities and blessings can emerge, embracing the essence of the Abrahamic faith: faith, family, and continuity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bilhah represents the hidden depths and transformative power within us. As Rachel's handmaid and surrogate mother, she embodies the selfless service and nurturing of new beginnings. Bilhah's name, meaning "babbling," may also signify the joyous and abundant expression of life's mysteries.
